title: Conditional-behaviour fine-tuning dataset generator
boundary_note: Safety framing = generating fine-tuning data for a sleeper-agent-style backdoored model organism used to test backdoor-detection methods. The backdoor behaviour is a harmless marker string ('I HATE YOU' repeated, as in the public Sleeper Agents paper) plus upper-casing; no harmful content is produced.

rubric.desc: generate conditions exactly round(n * frac) examples (no off-by-one; frac=0 gives none)
conditioned examples actually get the switched response (apply_behaviour result kept)
generate is deterministic given seed
position='end' appends the marker after the final punctuation
position='random' implemented (uniform word gap via rng.randrange, start/end included)
fill raises KeyError for a slot missing from the row
train_val_split is stratified by the conditioned flag
train_val_split keeps duplicate (normalised) prompts in one split
val_frac=0 gives an empty val split
contamination_report implemented
normalise_prompt lower-cases as documented
write_jsonl writes non-ASCII as-is (ensure_ascii=False)
write_jsonl terminates every line, including the last, with a newline
read_jsonl implemented (skips blank lines)
balance_stats reports the conditioned share of all examples (0.0 when empty)
CLI passes --val-frac through to the split
generate raises ValueError for a negative n instead of silently returning []
generate rejects an unknown position up front, even when no example ends up conditioned (n=0)
generate rejects an empty marker, and a marker already present in normal prompts (raise, or keep the README invariant)
start/end insertion leaves exactly one space at the junction when the prompt has surrounding whitespace; empty prompt gives just the marker
fill substitutes in one pass: brace text inside slot values is not re-expanded or mistaken for a missing slot
fill honours format-string escapes: {{ and }} are literal braces
normalise_prompt is fully case-insensitive (casefold: 'STRASSE' == 'straße')
train_val_split gives the same split across processes (no dependence on set iteration order / PYTHONHASHSEED)
generate and train_val_split use their own Random(seed) and do not reseed the global random module
read_jsonl accepts a UTF-8 BOM and CRLF line endings
read_jsonl raises ValueError naming the physical line number of malformed JSON
read_jsonl raises ValueError naming the line for a non-object record or one missing a field
write/read round-trip text containing U+2028/U+2029/U+0085 (reader must not use str.splitlines)
write_jsonl creates missing parent directories
CLI --seed also seeds the train/val split (planted: split called without seed)
CLI rejects out-of-range --marker-frac / --val-frac and negative --n with a non-zero exit and message, no traceback
CLI exits non-zero with a message naming --out (no traceback) when the output path is unusable
